steps.prompt: Work out $11 \times 11$, $12 \times 11$, $13 \times 11$. What pattern do you see in the digits?

cards.title: Split the digits, sum in the middle
cards.body: For a two-digit number times $11$, keep the first digit, put the sum of the two digits in the middle, and keep the last digit. $43 \times 11$: $4$, $4 + 3 = 7$, $3$, so $473$.

steps.text: $15$ is too big for one place: keep the $5$ in the middle and carry the $1$ to the $8$, making $9$.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: $\times 11 = \times 10 + \times 1$. $43 \times 11 = 430 + 43$. The tens digit of $430$ ($3$) and of $43$ ($4$) land in the same place and add: that is the middle sum.

prompts: Use $\times 11 = \times 10 + \times 1$ to explain the carry in $87 \times 11$.
